correctness.rationale: The proof determines the third-vertex atomic extension masks from every first and second flag, using the design identity \(r(k-1)=v-1\), \(r\ge k\) for \(k\ge3\), the no-four-cycle uniqueness property, and the strict closed-neighborhood inequality. The exceptional complete pair design on three points is a six-cycle, treated directly. A complete three-round back-and-forth lemma yields all within-class equivalences; explicit rank-three triangle and bad-edge sentences separate the three classes. The Fano flag count gives the sharp 21-vertex representative bound. Direct third-vertex enumeration and a separately written recursive EF-type computation confirm all tested classes; these checks are not used to infer the universal quantifier. \(J(7,3)\) has matching pair profiles and an induced claw, proving the sharp rank-four separator.

value.rationale: A natural entire class of finite block designs—including non-Desarguesian and non-flag-transitive instances, arbitrarily many points and arbitrarily large block sizes—collapses to three exact depth-three graph theories after passing to incidence-edge line graphs. The boundary \(k=2,v=3\) versus \(k=2,v\ge4\) versus \(k\ge3\) is complete and sharp; the minimal universal representative bound 21 is exact. The unexpected same-rank equivalence with \(J(7,3)\), despite a sharp four-round claw separator, gives an explicit structural limit on shallow first-order observation that is not merely a renamed counting exercise.
